subject: SLO pilot: reserved GPU sizing — action items & data request
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara@finlytics.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: SLO pilot: reserved GPU sizing — action items & data request

Hi Sara / Alex — great conversation earlier. Quick post-call recap and concrete asks so we can scope the dedicated pilot and sizing: 

Recap / goals
- FinLytics target: p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 150 ms for typical streaming flows (avg request size ~380 tokens; streaming response avg ~230 tokens).
- Peak sustained throughput target: 120 req/s with spikes to ~250 req/s for ~30s.
- Concurrency: bursts drive ~80 concurrent streaming clients; steady-state concurrency ~30.
- Availability: 24x7 reserved capacity for production pilot (with canary/burst to hosted pool as fallback).

Immediate asks from your side (what we need to size pilot):
1) Last 7 days traffic histogram (per-second QPS) and 95/99 token-length distributions (prompt + response).
2) Example streaming session (raw request + server-side timings if available) or synthetic sample payloads.
3) Confirmation of model variant you plan to use (model name + quantization if any).
4) Any regulatory constraints requiring on-prem/VPC-only setup.

Our proposal for the initial pilot (high level):
- 48–72 hour bench: run representative replay at your peak QPS with streaming enabled to validate p95 latency and tail behavior.
- Baseline hardware shortlist: H100 (low-latency streaming), A100 80GB (throughput), L4 (cost-optimized for non-critical batches).
- Start with 2x H100 equivalent capacity for latency-sensitive baseline, then expand to 3–4 units if throughput or headroom requires it.

Attached: pilot-test-plan.xlsx (layout, data requests, runbook).

Next steps
- Can you share the traffic histogram and a sample streaming session by EOD Wed (Aug 1)?
- We'll put Karthik on the pilot plan and Ben on ops/runbook for the bench run.

Thanks — I’ll schedule a quick kickoff after we get data.

—
Lauren Bishop
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: Sara Kim <sara@finlytics.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLO pilot: reserved GPU sizing — action items & data request

Thanks Lauren — consolidated answers below and attaching a short traffic export. Quoting your recap inline below for clarity.

On Mon, Jul 30, 2028 at 2:05 PM Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com> wrote:
> Recap / goals
> - FinLytics target: p95 end-to-end inference latency <= 150 ms for typical streaming flows (avg request size ~380 tokens; streaming response avg ~230 tokens).

This matches our internal SLO target — we’re aiming for p95 <= 150ms measured at the app edge (time from client request to first non-empty response chunk). A couple clarifications: our client is particularly sensitive to first-chunk latency during the streaming handshake.

Traffic & payloads (attached: finlytics_traffic_7d.csv)
- 7d peak sustained: 120 req/s (2pm PST weekdays).
- Burst observed: up to 260 req/s sustained for 20–40s during market opens.
- Token distribution (prompt+response): median 310, p95 620, p99 1,200.
- Streaming fraction: ~60% of requests stream; rest are single-shot generation.

Model & environment
- Primary model: openstream/fin-aug-13B (float16). We are open to quantized variants if you recommend them for latency/cost.
- Deploying in us-west-2 VPC; data residency okay in us-west region.

Procurement note
- We are prepared to commit to a month reserved if the pilot shows consistent p95 <= 150ms at our peak. Procurement needs a clear hardware recommendation + expected baseline token/sec cost for budgeting.

Actionables from our side
- Attached traffic export (CSV) and a single recorded streaming session (logs snippet) — see attachment stub.
- Confirmed: send recommended GPU shortlist + proposed pilot sizing/runbook by EOD Wed.

—
Sara Kim
Head of Platform Engineering, FinLytics
sara@finlytics.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sara Kim <sara@finlytics.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 12:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLO pilot: reserved GPU sizing — action items & data request

Thanks Sara — the traffic extract is perfect and confirms the distribution we discussed. A few quick, concrete recommendations ahead of the bench: 

Initial hardware shortlist & rationale
- H100 (2 units) — primary baseline for streaming-first workloads. H100 gives better single-request latency at scale and handles many concurrent KV/cache contexts well for 13B-class models. Good for first-chunk latency.
- A100 80GB (2 units) — alternative if you prioritize sustained throughput and larger batch aggregation; quantization can reduce memory footprint.
- L4/RTX-class (spot) — cost tier for non-critical batch/backfill workloads, not recommended for strict p95 latency.

Sizing & reserved throughput guidance (proposal)
- Baseline pilot: 2x H100 equivalent; expected steady-state support for ~100–140 req/s with p95 headroom ~20% depending on token lengths and batching configuration.
- Burst handling: configure autoscale policy to allow cloud-burst to a shared pool (hosted) for ephemeral spikes >200 req/s, with warm standby capacity.
- Concurrency tuning: set max concurrent streams per GPU to ~48 for H100 baseline, tune KV cache TTL and prefix caching for repeated prompts.

Bench plan notes
- We'll run a 48-hour replay at your peak profile. Key measurements: p50/p95/p99 first-chunk latency, total tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory headroom, and tail-blocking events.
- We'll test two configs: (A) 2xH100 low-latency mode (no aggressive batching) and (B) 2xA100 throughput mode (aggressive batching + dynamic batching windows).

Attachments: initial-benchnotes.csv (bench parameter matrix).

I'll prepare a short runbook and a resource estimate (cost tokens/sec) by EOD Wed and drop it into the Drive link Lauren shared. Ben — can you confirm ops availability week of Aug 7 to run the bench?

—
Karthik Iyer
Staff SRE (Inference) — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

2) Ben to confirm ops window for the 48h bench: tentatively Aug 7–8; Ben, please confirm by EOD Thu.
3) Sara / Alex: once you sign off on the hardware shortlist (H100 baseline vs A100 throughput), we’ll issue a pilot statement of work and a short procurement checklist.
4) I'll open the HubSpot mutual action plan and add the milestone: Pilot kickoff (Aug 7), Bench complete (Aug 9), Decision review (Aug 11). Link: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/DL-2028-4392

I’ll also attach the procurement-checklist.pdf for your procurement team. If FinLytics can commit to a month reserved after successful validation, we can fast-track pricing.

Thanks — looking forward to the bench.
